facts.text: Season and weather coverage means ensuring the system has been tested in all conditions it will meet, including rain, snow, fog, dust, mud, glare, dusk and darkness.
facts.quote: Season and weather coverage means making sure the system has been tested in all the conditions it will meet, including rain, snow, fog, dust, mud, glare, dusk and darkness

facts.text: The validation window of mid-2027 plus four months falls in northern summer and autumn and contains no northern cold season, so natural snow, freezing fog and low winter sun are absent.
facts.quote: A window of mid-2027 plus four months sits in the northern summer and autumn. It contains no northern cold season, so no natural snow, freezing fog or low winter sun

facts.text: Winter 2026 to 2027 is the last chance to collect snow and cold data from the existing warning fleet before validation.
facts.quote: The booklet calls the winter of 2026 to 2027 the last chance to collect snow and cold data from the existing warning fleet before validation

facts.text: Cameras lose contrast in rain and are blinded by glare and darkness.
facts.quote: Cameras lose contrast in rain and are blinded by glare and darkness

facts.text: Lidar scatters in fog and dust.
facts.quote: lidar scatters in fog and dust

facts.text: Radar responds to weather differently from cameras and lidar.
facts.quote: Weather hurts each sensor differently. Cameras lose contrast in rain and are blinded by glare and darkness; lidar scatters in fog and dust; radar behaves differently again

facts.text: Weather can make the ground slippery, changing stopping distance.
facts.quote: the ground becomes slippery, which changes stopping distance

facts.text: Dust is identified as the biggest off-road gap in sensor simulation.
facts.quote: Dust is named as the biggest off-road gap in sensor simulation

facts.text: There is no accepted score for how realistic a simulated weather effect is.
facts.quote: there is no accepted score for how real a simulated weather effect is

facts.text: Systematic breakdowns of collisions by light or weather were not found.
facts.quote: Systematic breakdowns of collisions by light or weather were not found

facts.text: Partial substitutes for natural seasonal weather coverage include component weather chambers, dust, fog and rain generated on a test track, southern-hemisphere sites during their winter, and fleet recordings from winter 2026 to 2027.
facts.quote: Partial substitutes exist: weather chambers for components (no specific off-road facility was found), dust, fog and rain generated on a test track, southern-hemisphere sites in their winter, and fleet recordings from the winter of 2026 to 2027

facts.text: No specific off-road facility for component weather-chamber testing was found.
facts.quote: weather chambers for components (no specific off-road facility was found)

facts.text: Natural seasonal weather is a validation constraint that no method can compress.
facts.quote: Natural seasonal weather is on the booklet's list of things no method can compress.

facts.text: Physical testing should be retained where simulation is weak.
facts.quote: The conclusion is to keep physical testing where simulation is weak

facts.text: Logging of the existing warning fleet should start now and continue through winter 2026 to 2027 to support weather validation.
facts.quote: to log the existing fleet through the winter starting now

facts.text: The first release should be restricted to an operating domain that excludes conditions not yet tested.
facts.quote: to release first in a domain that excludes the conditions not yet tested
